title: AI Implementation Roadmap
summary: A phased 90-day roadmap for rolling out AI from a bounded pilot to a trained team, with owners, guardrails, and success measures at each stage.
audience: Leaders and operators planning a controlled first 90 days of AI adoption.
assumptions: The first pilot is bounded and reversible
limitations: A generic 90-day plan must be adapted to organizational and regulatory context
Milestones do not guarantee successful adoption

title: AI Policy Starter Kit
summary: A plain-language internal AI-use policy template covering approved and prohibited uses, human review, confidentiality, and audit controls.
audience: Small teams preparing a first internal AI policy for qualified review.
methodology: Adapt every clause to real practice
assumptions: The template will be adapted and reviewed
The organization will train and enforce the resulting policy
limitations: The template is educational and is not legal advice
It cannot account for every jurisdiction, contract, or regulated use

title: AI Tool Evaluation Matrix
summary: A weighted matrix for comparing AI tools across capability, security, cost, usability, integration, and support so decisions rest on evidence rather than hype.
audience: Teams comparing AI products for a defined workflow.
methodology: Distinguish documented claims from observed performance
Require qualified security and legal review where needed
assumptions: The workflow and acceptance criteria are defined
Time-sensitive vendor information is independently verified
limitations: Scores depend on chosen weights and evidence quality
Products, pricing, policies, and model routing change

title: AI Use Case Inventory
summary: A worksheet for cataloging where AI could help a business and ranking candidates by value, effort, evidence, consequence, and readiness.
audience: Organizations beginning an AI opportunity and risk inventory.
assumptions: Workflow owners provide materially accurate information
Scores are reviewed rather than treated as automatic decisions
limitations: An inventory is not a technical or legal feasibility assessment
Incomplete workflow evidence can distort rankings

title: AI Workflow Mapping Worksheet
summary: Map a recurring workflow step by step, then identify where AI can assist, where humans retain authority, and where risk and evidence requirements live.
audience: Operators, consultants, and teams documenting workflows before introducing AI.
assumptions: People who perform the work participate
The map is validated against real examples
limitations: A diagram can omit tacit work and informal exceptions
Workflow suitability does not establish security, privacy, or compliance

title: Content Repurposing Workflow
summary: A repeatable workflow and prompt set for turning one strong source into a newsletter, social posts, short video scripts, and other channel-ready assets.
audience: Creators, founders, experts, and lean marketing teams repurposing source-grounded content.
methodology: Draft for one channel at a time
assumptions: The source is accurate and authorized for reuse
A human editor checks every derivative
limitations: The workflow cannot establish rights to third-party material
Condensation can remove nuance even when facts remain accurate

title: Meeting Summary Prompt Pack
summary: Copy-paste prompts that turn a meeting transcript into a summary, decision log, and owned action items while exposing missing names, dates, and ambiguities.
audience: Teams creating accountable records and follow-up from authorized meeting transcripts.
methodology: Mark missing information instead of guessing
assumptions: The transcript was lawfully and appropriately created
limitations: Transcripts can misidentify speakers or omit context
Recording, consent, confidentiality, and retention duties vary

title: SOP Prompt Pack
summary: Ten copy-paste prompts that turn a process in someone's head into a clear, testable standard operating procedure with uncertainty and human review built in.
audience: Owners, managers, operations leads, and teams documenting repeatable processes.
methodology: Ask one question at a time
assumptions: A knowledgeable human completes and validates the prompts
The resulting SOP is tested before adoption
limitations: Prompts cannot recover undisclosed tacit knowledge
High-stakes procedures require qualified legal, safety, financial, privacy, or regulatory review
